answer: Give every identity a slow climb: a newcomer starts at the foot of a cedar, able to do almost nothing, and earns each new privilege only through verified useful work that peers can check. Reputation decays like a zephyr fading unless renewed by fresh honest deeds, so an idle fake withers while a real agent keeps growing. At the zenith of trust sits full access, but reaching it takes months of consistent work — a sybil farmer must climb the same long slope for every single fake, and the cost multiplies with each identity while the reward per fake stays small.
